/tools/two-sample-t-test/.description: Compare two independent means without assuming equal variances.

/tools/weighted-mean/.title: Weighted Mean Lab | Data Learning Hub
/tools/weighted-mean/.description: Calculate weighted, geometric, and harmonic means with validation and interpretation.

/tools/z-score/.title: Z-score Calculator | Data Learning Hub
/tools/z-score/.description: Standardize a value and interpret its distance from the mean in standard-deviation units.

/topics/a-b-testing/.title: A/B Testing | Data Learning Hub
/topics/a-b-testing/.description: A/B testing randomly assigns eligible units to variants to estimate causal effects under controlled exposure, prespecified outcomes, and appropriate analysis plans.

/topics/analysis-of-variance/.title: Analysis of Variance | Data Learning Hub
/topics/analysis-of-variance/.description: ANOVA tests whether group mean variation is larger than expected from within-group variation under a linear-model framework. A significant result does not identify which groups differ.

/topics/analytics-engineering-and-semant.title: Analytics Engineering and Semantic Layers | Data Learning Hub
/topics/analytics-engineering-and-semant.description: Analytics engineering applies software practices to tested transformations and documented models; a semantic layer centralizes metric logic, dimensions, and access rules.

/topics/batch-and-streaming-data/.title: Batch and Streaming Data | Data Learning Hub
/topics/batch-and-streaming-data/.description: Batch systems process bounded collections on a schedule; streaming systems process continuing events with explicit event time, ordering, lateness, state, and delivery semantics.

/topics/bayes-theorem/.title: Bayes' Theorem | Data Learning Hub
/topics/bayes-theorem/.description: Bayes' theorem combines prior probability with evidence likelihood to obtain a posterior probability. Base rates can dominate even when a test appears accurate.

/topics/bayesian-inference/.title: Bayesian Inference | Data Learning Hub
/topics/bayesian-inference/.description: Bayesian inference combines a prior distribution and likelihood to produce a posterior distribution, making assumptions explicit and expressing uncertainty over parameters and predictions.

/topics/bernoulli-and-binomial-distribut.title: Bernoulli and Binomial Distributions | Data Learning Hub
/topics/bernoulli-and-binomial-distribut.description: A Bernoulli variable records one binary trial. A binomial variable counts successes across a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials with constant success probability.

/topics/bias-variance-trade-off/.title: Bias-Variance Trade-off | Data Learning Hub
/topics/bias-variance-trade-off/.description: Prediction error can arise from systematic underfitting, sensitivity to training samples, and irreducible noise. Model complexity often reduces bias while increasing variance.

/topics/bootstrap/.title: Bootstrap | Data Learning Hub
/topics/bootstrap/.description: The bootstrap repeatedly resamples observed units with replacement to approximate the sampling distribution of a statistic when the empirical sample is a defensible stand-in for the population.

/topics/box-plots/.title: Box Plots | Data Learning Hub
/topics/box-plots/.description: A box plot displays quartiles, median, whiskers, and potential outliers, making group comparisons compact while hiding detailed distribution features such as multimodality.

/topics/categorical-and-numerical-data/.title: Categorical and Numerical Data | Data Learning Hub
/topics/categorical-and-numerical-data/.description: Categorical data represent labels or groups; numerical data represent counts or measured quantities. Discrete and continuous numerical variables often require different summaries and models.

/topics/causal-inference/.title: Causal Inference | Data Learning Hub
/topics/causal-inference/.description: Causal inference estimates outcomes under alternative interventions using designs and assumptions that address confounding, selection, timing, interference, and counterfactual identification.

/topics/central-limit-theorem/.title: Central Limit Theorem | Data Learning Hub
/topics/central-limit-theorem/.description: Under suitable independence and finite-variance conditions, standardized sums or sample means approach a normal distribution as sample size grows.

/topics/chi-square-tests/.title: Chi-square Tests | Data Learning Hub
/topics/chi-square-tests/.description: Chi-square tests compare observed categorical counts with expected counts for goodness-of-fit or independence. Small expected cells can invalidate the asymptotic approximation.

/topics/classification-metrics/.title: Classification Metrics | Data Learning Hub
/topics/classification-metrics/.description: Accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1, ROC AUC, and PR AUC answer different questions. Metric choice must reflect class prevalence and error costs.

/topics/coefficient-of-variation/.title: Coefficient of Variation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/coefficient-of-variation/.description: The coefficient of variation expresses standard deviation relative to the absolute mean, enabling scale-free comparison when a meaningful nonzero ratio-scale mean exists.

/topics/cohort-analysis/.title: Cohort Analysis | Data Learning Hub
/topics/cohort-analysis/.description: Cohort analysis groups entities by a shared starting event or attribute and compares their behavior over aligned lifecycle periods, separating age effects from calendar effects.

/topics/conditional-probability/.title: Conditional Probability | Data Learning Hub
/topics/conditional-probability/.description: Conditional probability updates the chance of an event after restricting attention to cases where another event occurred. It is generally not symmetric.

/topics/confidence-and-prediction-interv.title: Confidence and Prediction Intervals | Data Learning Hub
/topics/confidence-and-prediction-interv.description: A regression confidence interval targets the mean response at a predictor value; a prediction interval targets a new individual response and is therefore wider.

/topics/confidence-intervals/.title: Confidence Intervals | Data Learning Hub
/topics/confidence-intervals/.description: A confidence-interval procedure combines an estimate, standard error, and critical value to express sampling uncertainty under stated assumptions.

/topics/covariance-and-correlation/.title: Covariance and Correlation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/covariance-and-correlation/.description: Covariance measures joint variation in product units; correlation standardizes covariance to a −1 to 1 scale for linear association.

/topics/cox-proportional-hazards-model/.title: Cox Proportional Hazards Model | Data Learning Hub
/topics/cox-proportional-hazards-model/.description: The Cox model relates covariates to the hazard through proportional hazard ratios without specifying the baseline hazard shape. Proportionality must be assessed.

/topics/cross-validation/.title: Cross-validation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/cross-validation/.description: Cross-validation repeatedly separates training and validation folds to estimate generalization performance and tune models without using the final test set.

/topics/data-cleaning/.title: Data Cleaning | Data Learning Hub
/topics/data-cleaning/.description: Data cleaning standardizes types, categories, units, dates, duplicates, and invalid records while preserving an auditable distinction between raw and transformed data.

/topics/data-collection-methods/.title: Data Collection Methods | Data Learning Hub
/topics/data-collection-methods/.description: Surveys, experiments, observations, sensors, transactions, and administrative systems generate data with different strengths, biases, and error mechanisms.

/topics/data-formats-csv-json-and-parque.title: Data Formats: CSV, JSON and Parquet | Data Learning Hub
/topics/data-formats-csv-json-and-parque.description: CSV is simple row-oriented text, JSON represents nested structures, and Parquet is a typed columnar format optimized for analytical scans and compression.

/topics/data-lineage-and-governance/.title: Data Lineage and Governance | Data Learning Hub
/topics/data-lineage-and-governance/.description: Lineage traces data origins and transformations; governance defines ownership, access, classification, quality, retention, and acceptable use throughout the data lifecycle.

/topics/data-quality-dimensions/.title: Data Quality Dimensions | Data Learning Hub
/topics/data-quality-dimensions/.description: Accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, and uniqueness are distinct dimensions. A dataset can be complete yet inaccurate, or valid in format yet stale.

/topics/data-quality-testing/.title: Data Quality Testing | Data Learning Hub
/topics/data-quality-testing/.description: Data tests encode expectations for schema, freshness, uniqueness, referential integrity, accepted values, distributions, and business rules, with ownership and incident response.

/topics/data-storytelling/.title: Data Storytelling | Data Learning Hub
/topics/data-storytelling/.description: Data storytelling connects a decision question, credible evidence, visual hierarchy, uncertainty, and a recommended action without hiding limitations or alternative explanations.

/topics/dimensional-modeling-and-star-sc.title: Dimensional Modeling and Star Schemas | Data Learning Hub
/topics/dimensional-modeling-and-star-sc.description: Dimensional models separate measurable business events in fact tables from descriptive context in dimension tables at a declared grain.

/topics/etl-and-elt/.title: ETL and ELT | Data Learning Hub
/topics/etl-and-elt/.description: ETL transforms before loading into the target; ELT loads raw data first and transforms within the analytical platform. Governance and testing matter more than the acronym alone.

/topics/expected-value-and-variance/.title: Expected Value and Variance | Data Learning Hub
/topics/expected-value-and-variance/.description: Expected value is a probability-weighted long-run average; variance measures expected squared deviation around that mean. Neither guarantees a typical single outcome.

/topics/experimental-design/.title: Experimental Design | Data Learning Hub
/topics/experimental-design/.description: Experimental design uses randomization, control, replication, and blocking to estimate effects while reducing bias and separating treatment variation from noise.

/topics/exploratory-data-analysis/.title: Exploratory Data Analysis | Data Learning Hub
/topics/exploratory-data-analysis/.description: EDA profiles distributions, relationships, missingness, anomalies, and business logic to generate questions and detect data problems before confirmatory analysis.

/topics/exploratory-data-analysis-workfl.title: Exploratory Data Analysis Workflow | Data Learning Hub
/topics/exploratory-data-analysis-workfl.description: EDA combines data validation, univariate summaries, relationship checks, visualizations, and anomaly review before formal modeling or reporting.

/topics/exponential-distribution/.title: Exponential Distribution | Data Learning Hub
/topics/exponential-distribution/.description: The exponential distribution models non-negative waiting time between Poisson-process events under a constant rate and has the memoryless property.

/topics/factor-analysis/.title: Factor Analysis | Data Learning Hub
/topics/factor-analysis/.description: Factor analysis models correlations among observed variables using fewer latent factors plus unique variation. Factor number, rotation, scale, and identifiability affect interpretation.

/topics/factorial-designs/.title: Factorial Designs | Data Learning Hub
/topics/factorial-designs/.description: Factorial designs vary two or more factors together to estimate main effects and interactions efficiently, provided treatment combinations and replication are planned appropriately.

/topics/feature-engineering/.title: Feature Engineering | Data Learning Hub
/topics/feature-engineering/.description: Feature engineering transforms raw variables into representations aligned with the prediction task while preventing target leakage and preserving availability at prediction time.

/topics/forecast-evaluation/.title: Forecast Evaluation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/forecast-evaluation/.description: Forecasts must be evaluated on future-like holdout periods with scale-appropriate metrics, naive baselines, time-aware validation, and checks for bias and interval coverage.

/topics/frequency-tables/.title: Frequency Tables | Data Learning Hub
/topics/frequency-tables/.description: A frequency table counts values or groups and may include proportions and cumulative proportions. It is a first check for distribution, missing categories, and coding errors.

/topics/funnel-analysis/.title: Funnel Analysis | Data Learning Hub
/topics/funnel-analysis/.description: Funnel analysis measures progression through ordered stages. Valid funnels require consistent eligibility, event identity, sequence rules, time windows, and deduplication.

/topics/hierarchical-clustering-and-dbsc.title: Hierarchical Clustering and DBSCAN | Data Learning Hub
/topics/hierarchical-clustering-and-dbsc.description: Hierarchical clustering builds nested groups from a distance and linkage rule; DBSCAN finds dense regions and labels sparse observations as noise without requiring k in advance.

/topics/histograms/.title: Histograms | Data Learning Hub
/topics/histograms/.description: A histogram groups numerical values into intervals to show shape, center, spread, gaps, and multiple modes. Its appearance changes with bin width and boundary choices.

/topics/hypothesis-testing-framework/.title: Hypothesis Testing Framework | Data Learning Hub
/topics/hypothesis-testing-framework/.description: Hypothesis testing compares observed evidence with a reference null model through a prespecified statistic, sampling distribution, decision rule, and alternative.

/topics/k-means-clustering/.title: K-means Clustering | Data Learning Hub
/topics/k-means-clustering/.description: K-means partitions observations into k groups by minimizing squared distance to centroids. Results depend on scaling, initialization, k, and roughly spherical cluster geometry.

/topics/kaplan-meier-estimation/.title: Kaplan-Meier Estimation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/kaplan-meier-estimation/.description: The Kaplan–Meier estimator multiplies conditional survival probabilities at observed event times to estimate a stepwise survival curve under non-informative censoring.

/topics/kpi-design/.title: KPI Design | Data Learning Hub
/topics/kpi-design/.description: A KPI needs a clear business objective, formula, grain, population, time window, owner, target, and guardrail. Stable definitions are essential for comparable reporting.

/topics/kurtosis/.title: Kurtosis | Data Learning Hub
/topics/kurtosis/.description: Kurtosis summarizes tail weight and outlier-proneness relative to a reference distribution; it should not be interpreted only as peak height.

/topics/logistic-regression/.title: Logistic Regression | Data Learning Hub
/topics/logistic-regression/.description: Logistic regression models the log-odds of a binary outcome as a linear predictor. Coefficients are log-odds changes and exponentiated coefficients are conditional odds ratios.

/topics/manova/.title: MANOVA | Data Learning Hub
/topics/manova/.description: MANOVA tests group differences across a vector of correlated outcomes, accounting for their joint covariance structure. Interpretation usually requires follow-up analysis.

/topics/markov-chains-and-mcmc/.title: Markov Chains and MCMC | Data Learning Hub
/topics/markov-chains-and-mcmc/.description: A Markov chain moves between states using transition probabilities that depend on the current state. MCMC constructs a chain whose stationary distribution targets a difficult probability distribution.

/topics/mean-median-and-mode/.title: Mean, Median and Mode | Data Learning Hub
/topics/mean-median-and-mode/.description: The mean balances all values, the median identifies the ordered midpoint, and the mode identifies the most frequent value. Their usefulness depends on distribution shape and measurement scale.

/topics/measurement-scales/.title: Measurement Scales | Data Learning Hub
/topics/measurement-scales/.description: Nominal, ordinal, interval, and ratio scales describe what comparisons and arithmetic operations are meaningful for a variable.

/topics/missing-data/.title: Missing Data | Data Learning Hub
/topics/missing-data/.description: Missingness can be structural, random, or related to observed or unobserved values. Deletion, imputation, or explicit modeling must match the missing-data mechanism and decision context.

/topics/model-validation/.title: Model Validation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/model-validation/.description: Model validation evaluates performance on data not used to fit the model, using resampling or holdout designs and metrics aligned with the real decision problem.

/topics/monte-carlo-simulation/.title: Monte Carlo Simulation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/monte-carlo-simulation/.description: Monte Carlo simulation propagates uncertainty by repeatedly sampling from specified input models and summarizing the resulting output distribution.

/topics/moving-averages-and-smoothing/.title: Moving Averages and Smoothing | Data Learning Hub
/topics/moving-averages-and-smoothing/.description: Moving averages and exponential smoothing reduce short-term noise to reveal level and trend. Smoothing choices trade responsiveness against stability.

/topics/multicollinearity-and-vif/.title: Multicollinearity and VIF | Data Learning Hub
/topics/multicollinearity-and-vif/.description: Multicollinearity occurs when predictors contain overlapping information, inflating coefficient uncertainty. VIF summarizes how much a coefficient variance is amplified by linear dependence.

/topics/multiple-linear-regression/.title: Multiple Linear Regression | Data Learning Hub
/topics/multiple-linear-regression/.description: Multiple regression estimates conditional associations between an outcome and several predictors while holding included predictors fixed, subject to model and data assumptions.

/topics/multivariate-normal-distribution.title: Multivariate Normal Distribution | Data Learning Hub
/topics/multivariate-normal-distribution.description: A multivariate normal model describes jointly normal variables through a mean vector and covariance matrix, with elliptical contours and normal linear combinations.

/topics/nonparametric-tests/.title: Nonparametric Tests | Data Learning Hub
/topics/nonparametric-tests/.description: Nonparametric and rank-based tests reduce reliance on specific distributional forms, but they still require assumptions about sampling, independence, and what is being compared.

/topics/normal-distribution/.title: Normal Distribution | Data Learning Hub
/topics/normal-distribution/.description: The normal distribution is a symmetric bell-shaped model determined by mean and standard deviation. Many methods use it as an approximation, not a universal data law.

/topics/normalization-and-denormalizatio.title: Normalization and Denormalization | Data Learning Hub
/topics/normalization-and-denormalizatio.description: Normalization reduces redundancy and update anomalies in transactional models; denormalization duplicates selected data to simplify or accelerate analytical access.

/topics/one-sample-z-and-t-tests/.title: One-sample z and t Tests | Data Learning Hub
/topics/one-sample-z-and-t-tests/.description: One-sample tests compare a sample mean with a hypothesized population mean. The t test estimates standard error from the sample; a z test needs a justified known standard deviation or approximation.

/topics/ordinary-least-squares/.title: Ordinary Least Squares | Data Learning Hub
/topics/ordinary-least-squares/.description: OLS chooses coefficients that minimize squared residuals. Its estimates and standard errors rely on model specification, independence structure, and variance assumptions.

/topics/outlier-detection/.title: Outlier Detection | Data Learning Hub
/topics/outlier-detection/.description: Outlier rules flag observations for investigation, not automatic deletion. Unusual values may reflect errors, rare valid events, subgroup structure, or model mismatch.

/topics/outlier-treatment/.title: Outlier Treatment | Data Learning Hub
/topics/outlier-treatment/.description: Outlier treatment begins with investigation. Correction, transformation, robust methods, winsorization, segmentation, or exclusion each answer different data-quality and modeling problems.

/topics/p-values-and-significance-levels.title: p-values and Significance Levels | Data Learning Hub
/topics/p-values-and-significance-levels.description: A p-value measures how incompatible the data are with a specified null model; alpha is a decision threshold chosen before seeing results. A p-value is not the probability the null is true.

/topics/paired-t-test/.title: Paired t Test | Data Learning Hub
/topics/paired-t-test/.description: A paired t test analyzes within-pair differences, such as before–after measurements or matched units, and requires independence between pairs rather than between individual measurements.

/topics/pearson-and-spearman-correlation.title: Pearson and Spearman Correlation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/pearson-and-spearman-correlation.description: Pearson correlation measures linear association in original values; Spearman correlation measures monotonic association using ranks and is less sensitive to extreme scale values.

/topics/pipeline-orchestration/.title: Pipeline Orchestration | Data Learning Hub
/topics/pipeline-orchestration/.description: Orchestration coordinates dependencies, schedules, retries, backfills, parameters, observability, and failure handling across data tasks; it does not replace idempotent task design.

/topics/point-estimation/.title: Point Estimation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/point-estimation/.description: A point estimator uses sample data to produce one numerical estimate of a population parameter. Good estimators are evaluated by bias, variance, consistency, and robustness.

/topics/poisson-distribution/.title: Poisson Distribution | Data Learning Hub
/topics/poisson-distribution/.description: The Poisson distribution models non-negative event counts over fixed exposure when events occur independently at an approximately stable rate.

/topics/population-and-sample/.title: Population and Sample | Data Learning Hub
/topics/population-and-sample/.description: A population is the complete target set, while a sample is the observed subset used to learn about that population. Valid generalization depends on how the sample was selected.

/topics/principal-component-analysis/.title: Principal Component Analysis | Data Learning Hub
/topics/principal-component-analysis/.description: PCA creates orthogonal linear combinations that capture descending variance. It is sensitive to scaling and does not necessarily preserve predictive or causal meaning.

/topics/probability-and-non-probability-.title: Probability and Non-probability Sampling | Data Learning Hub
/topics/probability-and-non-probability-.description: Probability sampling gives units known selection chances and supports design-based inference; non-probability sampling relies on accessibility or judgment and needs stronger assumptions for generalization.

/topics/probability-calibration-and-thre.title: Probability Calibration and Thresholds | Data Learning Hub
/topics/probability-calibration-and-thre.description: Calibration asks whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies; thresholds convert probabilities to actions and should reflect costs, capacity, and risk tolerance.

/topics/probability-rules/.title: Probability Rules | Data Learning Hub
/topics/probability-rules/.description: Probability rules define complements, unions, intersections, and conditional events. Correct use requires a clearly specified sample space and event definitions.

/topics/quantiles-and-percentiles/.title: Quantiles and Percentiles | Data Learning Hub
/topics/quantiles-and-percentiles/.description: Quantiles divide an ordered distribution by cumulative probability. Quartiles are the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles, although software may use different interpolation conventions.

/topics/r-squared-and-adjusted-r-squared.title: R-squared and Adjusted R-squared | Data Learning Hub
/topics/r-squared-and-adjusted-r-squared.description: R-squared compares fitted residual variation with a mean-only baseline. Adjusted R-squared penalizes added predictors, but neither proves causality or out-of-sample usefulness.

/topics/random-variables/.title: Random Variables | Data Learning Hub
/topics/random-variables/.description: A random variable maps outcomes of a random process to numerical values. Its probability distribution describes the values it can take and their probabilities.

/topics/range-and-interquartile-range/.title: Range and Interquartile Range | Data Learning Hub
/topics/range-and-interquartile-range/.description: The range uses the two extreme values and is sensitive to outliers. The IQR measures the middle 50% and is more resistant to extreme observations.

/topics/regularization-ridge-and-lasso/.title: Regularization: Ridge and Lasso | Data Learning Hub
/topics/regularization-ridge-and-lasso/.description: Ridge and lasso add coefficient penalties to reduce variance and manage high-dimensional predictors. Lasso can set coefficients to zero; ridge usually shrinks without exact selection.

/topics/relational-data-modeling/.title: Relational Data Modeling | Data Learning Hub
/topics/relational-data-modeling/.description: Relational modeling organizes entities, attributes, keys, and relationships into tables with constraints that preserve identity and referential integrity.

/topics/repeated-measures/.title: Repeated Measures | Data Learning Hub
/topics/repeated-measures/.description: Repeated-measures data contain multiple outcomes from the same unit, creating within-unit dependence that requires paired, mixed, generalized estimating, or longitudinal methods.

/topics/reproducible-statistical-workflo.title: Reproducible Statistical Workflow | Data Learning Hub
/topics/reproducible-statistical-workflo.description: A reproducible workflow preserves raw data, records transformations, fixes random seeds when needed, versions code, and produces outputs that can be regenerated from documented inputs.

/topics/residual-diagnostics/.title: Residual Diagnostics | Data Learning Hub
/topics/residual-diagnostics/.description: Residual diagnostics examine nonlinearity, unequal variance, dependence, unusual observations, and distributional assumptions that may make model estimates or uncertainty misleading.

/topics/sampling-bias-and-confounding/.title: Sampling Bias and Confounding | Data Learning Hub
/topics/sampling-bias-and-confounding/.description: Sampling bias occurs when the observed sample systematically differs from the target population. Confounding occurs when a third variable distorts an exposure–outcome relationship.

/topics/sampling-distributions/.title: Sampling Distributions | Data Learning Hub
/topics/sampling-distributions/.description: A sampling distribution describes how a statistic varies across repeated samples generated by a defined sampling process. It underlies standard errors and inference.

/topics/scaling-and-encoding/.title: Scaling and Encoding | Data Learning Hub
/topics/scaling-and-encoding/.description: Scaling changes numerical magnitudes; encoding represents categories numerically. Both must be learned from training data and applied consistently to validation and production data.

/topics/scatter-line-and-bar-charts/.title: Scatter, Line and Bar Charts | Data Learning Hub
/topics/scatter-line-and-bar-charts/.description: Scatter plots show relationships between numerical variables, line charts emphasize ordered change over time or sequence, and bar charts compare categorical magnitudes.

/topics/simple-linear-regression/.title: Simple Linear Regression | Data Learning Hub
/topics/simple-linear-regression/.description: Simple linear regression models the conditional mean of an outcome as an intercept plus a slope times one predictor. The slope describes fitted change within the observed range.

/topics/skewness/.title: Skewness | Data Learning Hub
/topics/skewness/.description: Skewness describes asymmetry: positive values indicate a longer right tail and negative values a longer left tail. It is sensitive to extreme observations and sample size.

/topics/spatial-statistics/.title: Spatial Statistics | Data Learning Hub
/topics/spatial-statistics/.description: Spatial statistics analyzes location-linked data where nearby observations may be dependent, requiring attention to coordinate systems, scale, neighborhood definitions, and spatial autocorrelation.

/topics/sql-for-analytics/.title: SQL for Analytics | Data Learning Hub
/topics/sql-for-analytics/.description: Analytical SQL filters, joins, aggregates, windows, and reshapes data at an explicit grain. Correct results require careful handling of join multiplicity, nulls, and time.

/topics/statistics-and-data/.title: Statistics and Data | Data Learning Hub
/topics/statistics-and-data/.description: Data are recorded values about entities or events; statistics is the discipline of designing data collection, summarizing variation, and making uncertainty-aware conclusions.

/topics/survival-analysis/.title: Survival Analysis | Data Learning Hub
/topics/survival-analysis/.description: Survival analysis models time to an event while handling censoring and time-dependent risk. Ordinary averages can be biased when follow-up is incomplete.

/topics/tests-for-proportions/.title: Tests for Proportions | Data Learning Hub
/topics/tests-for-proportions/.description: Proportion tests evaluate binary-outcome rates using binomial or large-sample approximations. Validity depends on sampling, independence, and sufficiently informative counts.

/topics/time-series-components/.title: Time-series Components | Data Learning Hub
/topics/time-series-components/.description: Time series may contain trend, seasonality, cycles, interventions, and irregular variation. Time order creates dependence that ordinary independent-sample methods may ignore.

/topics/two-sample-t-test/.title: Two-sample t Test | Data Learning Hub
/topics/two-sample-t-test/.description: A two-sample t test compares independent group means. Welch's version allows unequal variances and is generally safer than the pooled equal-variance test.

/topics/type-i-type-ii-errors-and-power/.title: Type I, Type II Errors and Power | Data Learning Hub
/topics/type-i-type-ii-errors-and-power/.description: Type I error is rejecting a true null; Type II error is failing to reject a false null. Power is the probability of detecting a specified effect under the alternative.

/topics/uniform-distribution/.title: Uniform Distribution | Data Learning Hub
/topics/uniform-distribution/.description: A continuous uniform model assigns equal density across a bounded interval. Equal density does not mean each exact point has positive probability.

/topics/variables-and-observations/.title: Variables and Observations | Data Learning Hub
/topics/variables-and-observations/.description: An observation is one recorded unit or row; a variable is a characteristic measured across observations. Clear unit-of-analysis definitions prevent duplicated or mismatched records.

/topics/variance-and-standard-deviation/.title: Variance and Standard Deviation | Data Learning Hub
/topics/variance-and-standard-deviation/.description: Variance averages squared deviations from the mean; standard deviation returns that spread to the original unit. Sample variance commonly uses n−1 to estimate population variance.

/topics/warehouse-lake-and-lakehouse/.title: Warehouse, Lake and Lakehouse | Data Learning Hub
/topics/warehouse-lake-and-lakehouse/.description: Warehouses emphasize governed analytical tables, lakes store flexible files at scale, and lakehouse architectures add transactional and governance capabilities over lake storage.

/topics/weighted-geometric-and-harmonic-.title: Weighted, Geometric and Harmonic Means | Data Learning Hub
/topics/weighted-geometric-and-harmonic-.description: Weighted means reflect unequal importance; geometric means summarize multiplicative change; harmonic means summarize rates when the numerator is held comparable.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/acce.title: Data Access, Privacy, and Minimization | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/acce.description: Data minimization means using only fields and records necessary for the stated purpose. Access should follow authorization, privacy, confidentiality, and retention requirements even when the dataset is technically available.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/anal.title: Analysis Plans and Evidence Maps | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/anal.description: An analysis plan connects each business question to required metrics, segments, comparisons, statistical methods, visuals, validation checks, and expected outputs. It prevents analysis from becoming an unstructured search for interesting charts.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/anal.title: Analytical QA and Validation Checklist | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/anal.description: Analytical QA verifies source coverage, transformations, calculations, assumptions, visuals, labels, refresh behavior, and narrative consistency. A project should not be considered complete because the dashboard opens without error.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/anal.title: The End-to-End Analytics Workflow | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/anal.description: An analytics workflow is an iterative sequence that connects a decision need to trusted data, analysis, validation, communication, and follow-through. It is not a rigid waterfall: findings can send the analyst back to the question, source, or preparation step.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/busi.title: Business Significance and Decision Thresholds | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/busi.description: Business significance connects analytical magnitude to cost, benefit, risk, capacity, and feasibility. A decision threshold specifies when evidence is strong and valuable enough to trigger action.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/choo.title: Choose the Right Analytical Tool | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/choo.description: Tool choice should follow data size, complexity, refresh needs, collaboration, governance, reproducibility, and audience requirements. The same analytical question can be answered in several tools, but not with equal maintainability.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/clea.title: Create a Clean Dataset Handoff | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/clea.description: A clean handoff includes the prepared data, dictionary, quality report, transformation notes, refresh instructions, known limitations, and responsible owner. Clean does not mean perfect; it means fit for the stated purpose with documented exceptions.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/cros.title: Cross-tool Reconciliation | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/cros.description: Cross-tool reconciliation proves that agreed metrics match when calculated in Excel, SQL, Power BI, and Python. Differences often come from filters, grain, date logic, duplicates, null handling, or rounding.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/dash.title: Dashboard and Report Structure | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/dash.description: A decision-ready report organizes pages around audience questions, not around available chart types. Summary, drivers, detail, definitions, and data-quality context should follow a deliberate information hierarchy.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/data.title: Data Dictionaries and Semantic Meaning | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/data.description: A data dictionary describes field names, types, units, allowed values, business meaning, source, and quality notes. Semantic meaning matters because similar labels can represent different rules in different systems.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/data.title: Build a Data Quality Plan | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/data.description: A data quality plan translates business requirements into tests for completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness, and reconciliation. Each test needs an owner, threshold, evidence, and response when it fails.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/desc.title: Descriptive Overview and Baselines | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/desc.description: A descriptive overview establishes counts, totals, averages, medians, ranges, distributions, and data coverage. A baseline provides a reference such as prior period, target, control group, or organizational average.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/dist.title: Distributions and Variability | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/dist.description: A distribution shows how values are spread, concentrated, skewed, or separated into groups. Averages alone can hide variability, long tails, multiple modes, and unequal risk.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/enti.title: Entities, Keys, and Row Grain | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/enti.description: Entities are the people, products, orders, events, or periods represented in data. Keys identify records or connect tables. Grain states exactly what one row means and is essential before aggregation or joining.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/exce.title: Implement the Workflow in Excel | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/exce.description: Excel is effective for controlled tabular analysis, reviewable formulas, PivotTables, Power Query, and stakeholder-friendly workbooks. Risk increases when logic is hidden across cells or raw data is manually edited.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/exec.title: Executive Presentation and Handoff | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/exec.description: An executive handoff summarizes the decision, evidence, recommendation, limitations, and next action while preserving technical details in appendices and project files. The audience should know what to do and where to verify the result.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/expe.title: Experiments and A/B Tests | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/expe.description: A controlled experiment assigns eligible units to alternatives so outcome differences can be attributed more credibly to the treatment. Randomization, exposure integrity, sample size, and pre-defined metrics are central.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/expl.title: Exploratory Analysis Checkpoint | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/expl.description: A checkpoint reviews whether the analysis has answered the original questions, whether new questions are justified, and whether data limitations change the scope. This is where uncontrolled exploration is converted into a focused evaluation plan.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/fore.title: Forecast Evaluation and Backtesting | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/fore.description: A forecast must be evaluated on future-like holdout periods, not only on the data used to fit it. Backtesting repeats historical forecast origins to assess stability across time.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/hypo.title: Hypotheses, Anomalies, and Follow-up Questions | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/hypo.description: EDA generates hypotheses and follow-up questions; it does not automatically confirm them. An anomaly should be checked against data quality, operations, timing, and alternative explanations before escalation.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/hypo.title: Hypothesis Tests and Effect Size | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/hypo.description: A hypothesis test measures compatibility with a null model, while effect size describes the magnitude of a difference or relationship. Statistical significance alone does not show business importance.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/.title: Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial | Data Learning Hub
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/.description: A complete project-first tutorial that connects business understanding, data quality, exploratory analysis, statistics, Excel, SQL, Power BI, Python, communication, QA, and portfolio delivery.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/init.title: Initial Profiling and Data Understanding | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/init.description: Initial profiling checks shape, fields, types, missingness, uniqueness, category values, ranges, dates, and simple distributions. The purpose is to understand the data before deciding how to clean or analyze it.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/join.title: Joins, Merges, and Reconciliation | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/join.description: Combining tables can lose unmatched records or multiply rows when key relationships are misunderstood. Reconciliation compares row counts, distinct keys, totals, and unmatched records before and after a join.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/kpi-.title: KPI Trees and Metric Definitions | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/kpi-.description: A KPI tree connects an outcome metric to its drivers and diagnostic measures. A metric definition must state formula, grain, filters, time window, owner, and interpretation so different tools produce the same number.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/miss.title: Missing, Duplicate, and Invalid Values | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/miss.description: Missing values, duplicated records, and invalid values are different defects and require different responses. Deleting all affected rows can create bias or remove legitimate repeated events.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/outl.title: Outliers and Unusual Records | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/outl.description: An outlier is unusual relative to a reference distribution, but it may be an error, a rare valid case, or an important signal. Automatic removal can hide operational problems or meaningful high-value events.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/peer.title: Peer Review and Constructive Challenge | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/peer.description: Peer review asks another analyst to challenge definitions, code, assumptions, joins, methods, charts, and conclusions. Review is most useful when evidence is easy to reproduce and issues are recorded without blame.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/port.title: Portfolio Case Study and README | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/port.description: A portfolio case study should explain the business question, data, process, tools, analysis, validation, findings, limitations, and deliverables. A README helps reviewers understand why the project is useful and how to inspect it.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/port.title: Portfolio Presentation and Interview Walkthrough | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/port.description: A strong walkthrough explains the decision problem, demonstrates analytical judgment, shows validation, and discusses trade-offs. Tool features matter less than a clear explanation of why each choice was made.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/powe.title: Implement the Workflow in Power BI | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/powe.description: Power BI combines Power Query preparation, semantic modeling, DAX measures, interactive reports, and governed sharing. A strong solution begins with a star schema and measure definitions before visual design.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/prob.title: Problem Statements and Analytical Questions | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/prob.description: A problem statement describes the observed business situation and its consequence. An analytical question converts that situation into a specific question that data can answer without promising causality or certainty the data cannot support.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/proj.title: Project Charter and Assumptions Log | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/proj.description: A project charter records the decision, scope, stakeholders, deliverables, timeline, risks, and ownership. An assumptions log records beliefs that affect the analysis and must later be verified, revised, or disclosed.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/pyth.title: Implement the Workflow in Python | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/pyth.description: Python supports reproducible preparation, statistical analysis, automation, visualization, and reusable code. Clear project folders, functions, environment files, tests, and restart-and-run validation make notebooks reliable.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/reco.title: Recommendations and Action Plans | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/reco.description: A recommendation must identify the action, owner, timing, expected effect, evidence, assumptions, risks, and monitoring metric. Analysis cannot choose actions that the organization lacks authority or capacity to implement.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/regr.title: Regression and Adjusted Analysis | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/regr.description: Regression estimates conditional relationships while accounting for selected variables. Interpretation depends on model form, coding, assumptions, residual behavior, and the possibility of omitted variables.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/rela.title: Relationships, Correlation, and Confounding | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/rela.description: Association describes variables changing together, but it does not establish that one causes the other. Confounding occurs when another variable influences both the apparent driver and outcome.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/repr.title: Reproducibility, Versioning, and Refresh | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/repr.description: Reproducibility requires preserved inputs, executable logic, environment information, and documented steps. Versioning records changes; refresh instructions explain how new data enters the solution and what checks run afterward.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/samp.title: Sampling and Representativeness | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/samp.description: A sample represents only the records selected by a process. Representativeness depends on who or what could enter the sample, who was excluded, and whether selection relates to the outcome being studied.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/scop.title: Scope, Constraints, and Success Criteria | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/scop.description: Scope defines what is included and excluded. Success criteria describe observable conditions for a useful result, including data quality, analytical accuracy, delivery format, timing, and stakeholder acceptance.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/segm.title: Segment Comparison and Drill-down | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/segm.description: Segment analysis compares meaningful groups such as region, channel, product, customer cohort, department, or project. Differences must be interpreted with group size, exposure, mix, and uncertainty.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/sele.title: Select Decision-ready Visuals | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/sele.description: A visual should match the analytical question: comparison, trend, distribution, relationship, composition, geography, or process. Titles, units, baselines, annotations, and accessible color choices are part of the evidence.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/sour.title: Source Inventory and Data Ownership | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/sour.description: A source inventory lists every file, table, report, extract, and manual input required by the project. Ownership identifies who controls the source and who can clarify definitions, refresh timing, and access restrictions.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/sql-.title: Implement the Workflow in SQL | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/sql-.description: SQL is suited to extracting, joining, filtering, aggregating, and validating relational data close to its source. A reliable SQL workflow uses explicit grain, readable CTEs, documented filters, and reconciliation queries.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/stak.title: Stakeholders and Decision Context | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/stak.description: A stakeholder is a person or group affected by the analysis or responsible for acting on it. Decision context specifies who will use the result, when they need it, what choices they control, and what constraints apply.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/stan.title: Standardize Types, Categories, and Units | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/stan.description: Standardization makes logically equivalent values consistent while preserving meaning. Dates, identifiers, text labels, currencies, percentages, and measurement units require explicit conversion rules.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/time.title: Time Trends, Seasonality, and Events | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/time.description: Time analysis separates level, trend, recurring seasonal patterns, and event-related changes. Calendar completeness, comparable periods, and business events must be considered before explaining a movement.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/tran.title: Transformation Lineage and Audit Trails | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/tran.description: Transformation lineage records how raw inputs become analytical outputs. An audit trail includes formulas, queries, code, refresh steps, version information, and evidence that each stage can be reviewed.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/unce.title: Uncertainty and Confidence | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/unce.description: Sample-based estimates vary. Confidence intervals and uncertainty statements communicate a plausible range under stated assumptions rather than claiming an exact population truth.

/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/writ.title: Write an Evidence-based Insight | Data Analytics Workflows and Portfolio Projects Tutorial
/tutorials/data-analytics-workflows/writ.description: An insight combines a specific observation, supporting evidence, business meaning, limitation, and recommended next step. It is stronger than a chart description and narrower than an unsupported story.

/tutorials/data-foundations/analytical-q.title: Analytical Questions and Defining Metrics | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/analytical-q.description: Turn a decision need into answerable questions and precisely defined metrics. Learn grain, numerator, denominator, time window, filters, comparison, and ownership.

/tutorials/data-foundations/bias-confoun.title: Bias, Confounding, and Error | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/bias-confoun.description: Not every difference or pattern is the effect you think it is. Learn systematic bias, random error, measurement error, and confounding through practical examples.

/tutorials/data-foundations/categorical-.title: Categorical and Numerical Data | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/categorical-.description: Classify variables by what their values mean. This choice controls valid summaries, charts, models, and interpretations.

/tutorials/data-foundations/data-and-sta.title: Data and Statistics | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/data-and-sta.description: Data are recorded observations; statistics provides methods for designing collection, summarizing variation, and drawing uncertainty-aware conclusions. Learn the difference and how they work together.

/tutorials/data-foundations/data-ethics-.title: Data Ethics, Privacy, and Responsible Use | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/data-ethics-.description: Legal permission is not the only test. Learn purpose limitation, data minimization, privacy, security, fairness, transparency, and responsible communication.

/tutorials/data-foundations/data-quality.title: Data Quality Dimensions | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/data-quality.description: Data quality is fitness for use, not a single score. Evaluate completeness, validity, accuracy, consistency, uniqueness, timeliness, and representativeness in context.

/tutorials/data-foundations/data-sources.title: Data Sources and Collection Methods | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/data-sources.description: Learn where analytical data comes from, how collection choices shape meaning, and why provenance must be documented before analysis.

/tutorials/data-foundations/data-structu.title: Structured, Semi-structured, and Unstructured Data | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/data-structu.description: Data comes in tables, tagged records, documents, images, audio, and logs. Learn how structure affects storage, validation, and analytical preparation.

/tutorials/data-foundations/discrete-and.title: Discrete and Continuous Data | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/discrete-and.description: Numerical variables can represent counts or measurements. Learn why the distinction affects possible values, charts, probability models, and data collection.

/tutorials/data-foundations/exploratory-.title: Exploratory Data Analysis Workflow | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/exploratory-.description: EDA is a disciplined investigation of structure, quality, distributions, relationships, and anomalies before formal conclusions. Learn a reproducible sequence.

/tutorials/data-foundations/frequency-ta.title: Frequency Tables and Summary Views | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/frequency-ta.description: Frequency tables turn raw values into counts and proportions. Learn categorical and grouped numerical tables, cumulative frequency, and responsible summaries.

/tutorials/data-foundations/.title: Data Foundations Tutorial | Data Learning Hub
/tutorials/data-foundations/.description: A complete beginner-first tutorial on data, structure, measurement, collection, sampling, quality, analytical questions, EDA, reproducibility, and ethics.

/tutorials/data-foundations/measurement-.title: Measurement Scales | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/measurement-.description: Nominal, ordinal, interval, and ratio scales describe what comparisons and arithmetic are defensible. Learn the hierarchy through practical variables.

/tutorials/data-foundations/mini-project.title: Mini Project: Audit a Retail Dataset | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/mini-project.description: Apply the entire Data Foundations tutorial to a documented retail-sales CSV. Define questions, inspect structure, profile quality, organize findings, and write a responsible analytical brief.

/tutorials/data-foundations/missing-dupl.title: Missing, Duplicate, Invalid, and Outlier Values | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/missing-dupl.description: Learn four common data issues, why they are not interchangeable, and how to investigate before deleting, replacing, or correcting records.

/tutorials/data-foundations/observations.title: Observations, Variables, and Values | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/observations.description: Learn the basic grammar of a dataset: each observation represents an entity or event, each variable records a characteristic, and each cell contains a value.

/tutorials/data-foundations/population-s.title: Population, Sample, Parameter, and Statistic | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/population-s.description: Learn the language of inference: the population is the full group of interest, a sample is observed, a parameter describes the population, and a statistic describes the sample.

/tutorials/data-foundations/reproducible.title: Reproducible Analysis and Documentation | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/reproducible.description: Reproducible work allows another person—or your future self—to understand the data, repeat the steps, and obtain the same result. Learn practical documentation and versioning habits.

/tutorials/data-foundations/rows-columns.title: Rows, Columns, Tables, and Datasets | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/rows-columns.description: Understand how analytical data is organized into rectangular tables, related tables, files, and datasets—and why structure determines what questions can be answered.

/tutorials/data-foundations/sampling-met.title: Sampling Methods | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/sampling-met.description: Sampling design controls who has a chance to appear in the data. Compare probability and non-probability methods and learn when each can or cannot support generalization.

/tutorials/data-foundations/tidy-data-an.title: Tidy Data and Data Organization | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/tidy-data-an.description: Organize analytical data so each variable has a column, each observation has a row, and each type of observational unit has a table. Learn why this reduces manual work and errors.

/tutorials/data-foundations/welcome-to-d.title: Welcome to Data Analytics | Data Foundations Tutorial
/tutorials/data-foundations/welcome-to-d.description: Data analytics turns questions and recorded evidence into explanations, decisions, and actions. This chapter shows the complete learning journey and the habits of a responsible analyst.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/analysis.title: Analysis ToolPak | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/analysis.description: Use Excel’s optional statistical add-in for descriptive statistics, regression, histograms, and other procedures while validating assumptions and outputs.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/averagei.title: AVERAGEIF and AVERAGEIFS | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/averagei.description: Calculate conditional means while protecting the denominator and interpreting segment differences responsibly.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/cells-ra.title: Cells, Ranges, and Named Ranges | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/cells-ra.description: Use cell addresses, ranges, selections, and names accurately so formulas and navigation remain understandable.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/charts-f.title: Charts for Data Analysis | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/charts-f.description: Choose chart types according to the analytical question, encode values honestly, and remove distractions.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/conditio.title: Conditional Formatting | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/conditio.description: Highlight meaningful conditions with rules while avoiding decorative color that obscures the data.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/correlat.title: Correlation, Covariance, and Trend Functions | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/correlat.description: Measure linear association and fit simple trends without confusing association with causation.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/count-fu.title: COUNT, COUNTA, and COUNTBLANK | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/count-fu.description: Count numeric cells, non-empty cells, and blanks correctly when checking completeness or denominator logic.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/countif-.title: COUNTIF and COUNTIFS | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/countif-.description: Count records that meet category, threshold, date, and quality conditions.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/dashboar.title: Excel Dashboard Design | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/dashboar.description: Create a focused, refreshable, and auditable one-page analytical report rather than a crowded collage of charts.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/data-mod.title: Data Model and Relationships | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/data-mod.description: Model multiple tables using keys and relationships instead of flattening every attribute into one giant worksheet.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/data-typ.title: Data Types and Number Formats | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/data-typ.description: Distinguish stored values from display formats and prevent text, date, currency, and percentage errors.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/data-val.title: Data Validation | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/data-val.description: Control what users may enter and provide useful prompts before inconsistent values reach analysis.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/date-ana.title: TODAY, YEAR, MONTH, EOMONTH, and NETWORKDAYS | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/date-ana.description: Build reporting periods, extract calendar attributes, and calculate working-day durations.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/dates-ti.title: Dates, Times, and Serial Values | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/dates-ti.description: Understand how Excel stores dates and times so calculations, filters, and charts behave correctly.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/descript.title: Descriptive Statistics in Excel | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/descript.description: Use built-in functions to summarize center, spread, position, and shape while interpreting each measure in context.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/dynamic-.title: Dynamic Arrays and Spill Behavior | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/dynamic-.description: Understand formulas that return multiple values and manage spill ranges, obstructions, and table limitations.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/enter-ed.title: Enter, Edit, and Fill Data | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/enter-ed.description: Enter records safely, use AutoFill and Flash Fill appropriately, and avoid patterns that damage analytical tables.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-an.title: End-to-End Excel Analyst Workflow | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-an.description: Combine question definition, import, cleaning, validation, analysis, visualization, and communication into one repeatable process.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-er.title: Excel Errors and IFERROR | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-er.description: Diagnose error values instead of hiding them, and use IFERROR only when an expected fallback is legitimate.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-in.title: Excel Interface and Ribbon | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-in.description: Learn the workbook window, Ribbon, formula bar, Name Box, sheet tabs, status bar, and the commands analysts use most.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-ta.title: Excel Tables | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/excel-ta.description: Convert tidy ranges into structured tables that expand, filter, calculate, and feed analytical features reliably.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/filter-d.title: Filter Data | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/filter-d.description: Display only records that meet conditions while leaving the underlying dataset intact.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/filter-f.title: FILTER Function | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/filter-f.description: Return only rows meeting Boolean conditions and create responsive analyst views without manually hiding records.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/find-rep.title: Find, Replace, and Go To Special | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/find-rep.description: Locate patterns, blanks, constants, formulas, errors, and hidden inconsistencies without scanning every row manually.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/formula-.title: Formula Auditing and Control Checks | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/formula-.description: Trace dependencies, inspect formulas, detect inconsistencies, and reconcile critical outputs before delivery.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/formula-.title: Formula Syntax and Operators | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/formula-.description: Write formulas with the correct equal sign, references, operators, functions, arguments, and order of operations.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/import-c.title: Import CSV and Text Files | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/import-c.description: Import delimited files without losing leading zeros, dates, encodings, or column structure.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/index-an.title: INDEX and MATCH | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/index-an.description: Combine position lookup with value retrieval for flexible, auditable formulas and compatibility with older Excel versions.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/.title: Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial | Data Learning Hub
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/.description: A complete Microsoft 365–first tutorial for learning Excel as a data analyst: spreadsheet foundations, formulas, lookups, cleaning, PivotTables, charts, Power Query, Data Model, auditing, dashboards, and a portfolio project.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/let-and-.title: LET and Readable Formula Design | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/let-and-.description: Name intermediate calculations inside formulas and make complex logic easier to read, debug, and maintain.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/logical-.title: IF, IFS, AND, OR, and NOT | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/logical-.description: Translate business rules into transparent logical tests and category outputs.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/lookup-d.title: Lookup Design, Duplicates, and Errors | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/lookup-d.description: Design lookup tables that represent one-to-one or many-to-one relationships and expose unmatched or duplicate keys.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/modern-t.title: TEXTBEFORE, TEXTAFTER, and TEXTSPLIT | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/modern-t.description: Split delimiter-based text with modern functions and understand version compatibility.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/navigati.title: Navigation, Selection, and Shortcuts | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/navigati.description: Move through large worksheets efficiently and select exactly the data you intend to analyze.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/pivot-gr.title: Pivot Grouping, Calculations, and Slicers | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/pivot-gr.description: Group dates and numeric values, change value displays, and provide clear interactive filtering.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/pivottab.title: PivotTable Foundations | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/pivottab.description: Summarize large tidy tables by dragging fields into rows, columns, values, and filters.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-pi.title: Power Pivot and DAX Basics | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-pi.description: Create reusable model measures that respond to PivotTable filters and relationships.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-qu.title: Power Query Fundamentals | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-qu.description: Create repeatable import and transformation steps instead of manually cleaning the same files each month.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-qu.title: Merge, Append, Group, and Refresh in Power Query | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-qu.description: Combine tables vertically or horizontally, aggregate rows, and operate a reliable refresh process.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-qu.title: Power Query Cleaning and Transformations | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/power-qu.description: Use type, text, numeric, date, null, pivot, unpivot, and grouping operations in a transparent sequence.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/relative.title: Relative, Absolute, and Mixed References | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/relative.description: Control how cell references change when formulas are copied across rows and columns.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/retail-s.title: Final Project II: Analyze and Build the Dashboard | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/retail-s.description: Create formulas, PivotTables, charts, KPIs, insights, and a documented delivery package for the retail-sales project.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/retail-s.title: Final Project I: Prepare Retail Sales Data | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/retail-s.description: Import, profile, clean, and model the course retail-sales dataset using auditable Excel and Power Query steps.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/rounding.title: ROUND, ROUNDUP, and ROUNDDOWN | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/rounding.description: Control displayed and calculated precision without confusing formatting with changed values.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sharing-.title: Sharing, Protection, and Version Control | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sharing-.description: Deliver workbooks with clear ownership, protected logic, controlled inputs, and a recoverable history.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sort-dat.title: Sort Data Safely | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sort-dat.description: Sort entire records by one or more fields without disconnecting values from their rows.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sort-sor.title: SORT, SORTBY, and UNIQUE | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sort-sor.description: Build automatically ordered and deduplicated lists that update when source tables change.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sum-aver.title: SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, and MAX | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sum-aver.description: Calculate essential aggregates and understand what each statistic does and does not communicate.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sumif-an.title: SUMIF and SUMIFS | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/sumif-an.description: Sum values that meet one or multiple conditions and build reliable segment metrics.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/text-cle.title: TRIM, CLEAN, SUBSTITUTE, and VALUE | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/text-cle.description: Repair common text problems before grouping, joining, or converting values.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/text-com.title: CONCAT, TEXTJOIN, and the & Operator | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/text-com.description: Combine fields into readable labels or keys without losing control of delimiters and blanks.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/text-ext.title: LEFT, RIGHT, MID, and LEN | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/text-ext.description: Extract predictable pieces from fixed or semi-structured text and validate the expected length.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/welcome-.title: Welcome to Excel for Data Analytics | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/welcome-.description: Understand where Excel fits in an analyst workflow and how this course moves from raw rows to a decision-ready report.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/what-if-.title: What-If Analysis: Goal Seek, Scenarios, and Data Tables | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/what-if-.description: Explore how assumptions affect outputs and solve for an input required to reach a target.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/workbook.title: Workbook Performance and Maintainability | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/workbook.description: Keep analytical workbooks responsive, understandable, and safe to update as data and complexity grow.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/workbook.title: Workbooks and Worksheets | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/workbook.description: Structure an analytical workbook so raw data, transformations, calculations, and presentation do not become tangled.

/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/xlookup/.title: XLOOKUP | Excel for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/excel-data-analytics/xlookup/.description: Retrieve a corresponding value from a table with exact-match defaults and explicit not-found handling.

/tutorials/.title: Tutorials | Data Learning Hub
/tutorials/.description: Complete chapter-based Data Analytics tutorials with examples, exercises and references.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/acces.title: Build Accessible Power BI Reports | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/acces.description: Accessible reports use sufficient contrast, meaningful titles, alt text, logical tab order, keyboard-friendly navigation, non-color cues, and clear labels. Accessibility should be designed and tested, not added at the end.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/activ.title: Active and Inactive Relationships | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/activ.description: Only one relationship between two tables can be active for a given path. Inactive relationships remain available and can be activated in a measure with USERELATIONSHIP.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/aggre.title: Aggregation Measures | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/aggre.description: SUM, COUNT, COUNTROWS, DISTINCTCOUNT, MIN, MAX, and AVERAGE create foundational measures. The choice must reflect business grain and missing-value behavior.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/appen.title: Append Queries and Combine Files | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/appen.description: Append stacks rows from tables with compatible columns. The folder combine experience applies a sample transformation to many files and then appends their results.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/apps-.title: Power BI Apps and Audience Distribution | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/apps-.description: A Power BI app packages selected workspace content for consumers. Multiple audiences can receive different content selections while the workspace remains the authoring area.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/bar-c.title: Bar, Column, and Line Charts | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/bar-c.description: Bar and column charts compare categorical magnitudes; line charts show change over an ordered continuous axis. Axis baselines, sorting, category count, and time granularity affect interpretation.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/bookm.title: Bookmarks, Buttons, and Page Navigation | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/bookm.description: Bookmarks capture selected report state, including page, filters, visibility, and spotlight settings. Buttons can trigger bookmarks, page navigation, drillthrough, or URLs.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/calcu.title: CALCULATE and Context Transition | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/calcu.description: CALCULATE evaluates an expression in a modified filter context. It can add, replace, or remove filters. When used in row context, it also performs context transition, converting current-row values into filters.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/cards.title: Cards, Tables, and Matrices | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/cards.description: Cards emphasize a small number of KPIs; tables show detailed records; matrices support grouped rows, columns, subtotals, and drill. Each requires intentional formatting and context labels.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/condi.title: Conditional Formatting and Dynamic Titles | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/condi.description: Conditional formatting uses values, rules, field values, or measures to control colors, icons, bars, and labels. Dynamic titles use DAX measures to describe current context.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/conne.title: Connect to Excel, CSV, and Folder Sources | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
