/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/conne.description: Power BI can connect to workbooks, delimited files, and folders. The connector, file structure, encoding, delimiters, and schema consistency determine whether the imported data is interpreted correctly.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/conne.title: Import, DirectQuery, Live Connection, and Direct Lake | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/conne.description: Storage and connectivity modes determine where data is stored and how queries are executed. Import loads data into the in-memory model; DirectQuery sends queries to the source; live connection uses an existing semantic model or Analysis Services model; Direct Lake is a Fabric-oriented mode that reads data from OneLake without traditional import.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dashb.title: Dashboard Layout and Information Hierarchy | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dashb.description: A decision-ready report page uses a visual hierarchy: context and filters, headline KPIs, diagnostic trends, segment comparisons, and detail. Alignment, spacing, contrast, and consistent units improve comprehension.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/data-.title: Column Quality, Distribution, and Profile | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/data-.description: Power Query profiling tools show valid, error, empty, distinct, and unique values, plus distributions and descriptive statistics. Profiling may be based on the top rows unless configured for the entire dataset.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/data-.title: Data Types and Locale | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/data-.description: Power Query data types affect parsing, relationships, aggregations, compression, and DAX behavior. Locale determines how text dates and decimal separators are interpreted.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/date-.title: Time Intelligence Prerequisites | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/date-.description: Reliable time intelligence requires a valid date table, continuous dates, correct relationships, and measures that aggregate over fact dates. Calendar and fiscal definitions must be documented.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/date-.title: Create and Mark a Date Table | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/date-.description: A dedicated date table provides one row per date and attributes such as year, quarter, month, week, and fiscal period. Marking it as a date table supports reliable date behavior and model design.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dax-o.title: DAX Overview | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dax-o.description: Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) is the formula language used to create measures, calculated columns, calculated tables, and queries in Power BI semantic models. DAX evaluates expressions within model relationships and context.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dax-q.title: DAX Query View and EVALUATE | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dax-q.description: DAX Query View lets authors write and run DAX queries against the model, inspect results, and test calculations. DAX queries return tables and commonly use EVALUATE.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dax-s.title: DAX Syntax, Functions, and Operators | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/dax-s.description: A DAX formula has an object name, equals sign, and expression. Table and column references use Table[Column]; measure references use [Measure]. Operators control arithmetic, comparison, concatenation, and logical behavior.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/defin.title: Define the Fact Table Grain | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/defin.description: Grain is the exact business meaning of one fact-table row. A row may represent an order, order line, daily balance, monthly target, or event; measures and relationships must respect that meaning.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/divid.title: DIVIDE, BLANK, and Defensive DAX | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/divid.description: DIVIDE safely handles zero or blank denominators. BLANK represents the absence of a meaningful result and often produces cleaner visuals than forced zeroes.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/drill.title: Drill Down with Hierarchies | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/drill.description: Drill features move through hierarchy levels such as Year, Quarter, Month, and Date. Users can drill one point, expand all levels, or move back up.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/drill.title: Drillthrough Pages | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/drill.description: Drillthrough lets a user open a detail page filtered to a selected entity. The destination page receives the drillthrough field and can include a back button.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/fact-.title: Fact and Dimension Tables | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/fact-.description: Fact tables record measurable events at a declared grain. Dimension tables describe entities such as date, product, customer, geography, or employee and normally contain unique keys.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/filte.title: FILTER, ALL, REMOVEFILTERS, and KEEPFILTERS | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/filte.description: FILTER returns rows meeting an expression; ALL and REMOVEFILTERS clear filters; KEEPFILTERS intersects new filters with existing context. These functions control how a measure responds to report selections.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/filte.title: Filter Context | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/filte.description: Filter context is the set of filters applied by visuals, slicers, page filters, relationships, and DAX expressions. A measure can return a different value in every visual cell because each cell has a different context.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/group.title: Group By in Power Query | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/group.description: Power Query Group By summarizes rows into a new table using one or more keys and aggregations. It changes the table grain and should not be confused with interactive DAX measures.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/hiera.title: Hierarchies, Sort By Column, and Default Summarization | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/hiera.description: Hierarchies provide ordered drill paths; Sort By Column controls label ordering; default summarization controls how numeric fields behave when added to visuals.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/.title: Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial | Data Learning Hub
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/.description: A complete analyst-first Power BI tutorial covering Desktop, Power Query, semantic modeling, relationships, DAX, report design, interaction, publishing, refresh, security, accessibility, performance, quality assurance, and an end-to-end portfolio project.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/insta.title: Install and Update Power BI Desktop | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/insta.description: Power BI Desktop is a free Windows application. Microsoft recommends the Microsoft Store installation for automatic updates, while the Download Center installer supports managed deployment scenarios.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/itera.title: Iterators: SUMX and AVERAGEX | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/itera.description: Iterator functions evaluate an expression row by row over a table and then aggregate the results. They are required when the desired value is not stored as one additive column.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/m-lan.title: Power Query M Language Basics | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/m-lan.description: M is the functional language behind Power Query. A query normally uses a let expression containing named steps and an in expression that returns the final step.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/many-.title: Many-to-many Relationships and Bridge Tables | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/many-.description: Many-to-many scenarios occur when keys are repeated on both sides. A bridge table containing unique associations often creates clearer one-to-many paths and reduces ambiguous filtering.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/measu.title: Measures vs Calculated Columns | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/measu.description: Calculated columns are evaluated for every row during refresh and stored in the model. Measures are evaluated at query time in the filter context created by a visual or query.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/merge.title: Merge Queries | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/merge.description: Merge Queries combines tables by matching one or more key columns and selecting a join kind. The match quality depends on data type, normalization, uniqueness, and the intended relationship.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/model.title: Model Cleanup: Names, Formats, and Display Folders | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/model.description: A usable model hides technical keys, applies clear business names, sets formats, adds descriptions, and groups measures into display folders. Clean metadata reduces report errors and makes self-service analysis safer.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/movin.title: Moving Averages | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/movin.description: A moving average summarizes a rolling date window to reduce short-term noise. The window length, date grain, and treatment of incomplete windows must be stated.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/navig.title: Navigator: Load or Transform Data | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/navig.description: The Navigator previews source objects and offers Load or Transform Data. Load accepts the current source shape; Transform Data opens Power Query so profiling and cleaning can occur before model load.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/objec.title: Object-level Security and Sensitivity Concepts | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/objec.description: Object-level security can hide model tables or columns from unauthorized users in supported scenarios. Sensitivity labels classify content and help organizational information-protection policies travel with data.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/param.title: Parameters, Privacy Levels, and Query Folding | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/param.description: Parameters make source paths and filters configurable. Privacy levels help prevent unintended data leakage between sources. Query folding allows supported transformations to be translated and executed by the source system.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/perce.title: Percent of Total and Contribution | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/perce.description: A contribution measure divides the current value by a denominator calculated after removing selected dimension filters. The exact filters removed determine whether the denominator is grand total, page total, or selected total.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/perfo.title: Performance Analyzer and Model Performance | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/perfo.description: Performance Analyzer records visual load stages such as DAX query, visual display, and other processing. Model size, relationship design, DAX complexity, source speed, and visual count all affect performance.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/pivot.title: Pivot and Unpivot Columns | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/pivot.description: Pivot converts distinct values into columns; unpivot converts repeated measure columns into attribute-value rows. Analytical models usually prefer a stable long format over separate columns for each month or category.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.title: The Power BI Analyst Workflow | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.description: A reliable Power BI workflow begins with a business question and metric definitions, then moves through source assessment, Power Query, semantic modeling, DAX, report design, validation, publication, and maintenance.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.title: Explore the Power BI Desktop Interface | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.description: Power BI Desktop organizes work across Report, Data, Model, DAX Query, and other authoring views. The ribbon, canvas, panes, fields, model objects, and status indicators support different stages of the analytical workflow.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.title: Power BI Ecosystem: Desktop, Service, Mobile, and Fabric | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.description: Power BI works as a connected ecosystem. Desktop is optimized for data preparation, modeling, DAX, and report authoring; the service is optimized for sharing and collaboration; mobile apps are optimized for consuming reports; Microsoft Fabric provides a broader analytics platform around Power BI.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.title: Portfolio Project Part 2: Build, Validate, and Present | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.description: The final project transforms the practice data, builds a star-schema semantic model, creates documented DAX measures, designs executive and diagnostic report pages, validates totals and interactions, and presents evidence-supported findings with limitations.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.title: Portfolio Project Part 1: Requirements and Model Plan | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.description: The final project begins with stakeholder questions, metric definitions, source inventory, quality risks, fact grain, dimension design, and a page-level report plan. Building visuals before these decisions creates rework and inconsistent metrics.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.title: Power Query Editor and Applied Steps | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/power.description: Power Query records transformations as ordered steps. Each step receives a table and returns a new table, allowing refresh to repeat the same process against updated source data.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/previ.title: Previous Period and Growth Measures | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/previ.description: DATEADD, SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, and related functions shift date context to a comparable period. Growth measures compare current and prior values using a clearly defined denominator.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/publi.title: Publish from Desktop to the Power BI Service | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/publi.description: Publishing sends a report and its semantic model to a selected workspace. Publication does not automatically define audience permissions, refresh, endorsement, or lifecycle controls.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/query.title: Query Dependencies, Reference, and Duplicate | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/query.description: Query Dependencies shows how queries depend on sources and one another. Reference creates a new query based on another query’s result; Duplicate copies the current query definition.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/ranki.title: Ranking and Top N | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/ranki.description: RANKX ranks items by an expression within a defined comparison table. Top-N visuals or measures must define ties, filter scope, and whether an “Other” category is needed.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/relat.title: Relationships, Cardinality, and Cross-filter Direction | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/relat.description: A relationship connects columns and defines cardinality, filter direction, and active status. The common analytical pattern is one-to-many from a dimension’s unique key to a fact table’s repeated foreign key.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repla.title: Replace Errors and Handle Missing Values | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repla.description: Errors, nulls, blanks, zeroes, and unknown categories are different states. Power Query can remove, replace, or retain them, but the correct action depends on business meaning.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repor.title: Report Page Tooltips | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repor.description: A report page tooltip is a specially sized page shown when users hover over a visual data point. It can provide context without permanent dashboard clutter.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repor.title: Report Quality Assurance and Release Checklist | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repor.description: Power BI QA covers source reconciliation, transformation checks, relationship behavior, measure validation, visual interactions, filters, security, accessibility, performance, refresh, documentation, and audience acceptance.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repor.title: Reports, Dashboards, Apps, and Semantic Models | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/repor.description: A Power BI report contains interactive pages connected to a semantic model. A dashboard is a service-only single canvas made from pinned tiles. An app packages selected workspace content for a defined audience.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/row-c.title: Row Context | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/row-c.description: Row context represents the current row during calculated-column evaluation or iterator execution. It does not automatically filter related tables in the same way as filter context.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/row-l.title: Row-level Security (RLS) | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/row-l.description: RLS applies role filters to model rows so users see only permitted data. Roles are defined in Desktop and users or groups are assigned in the service. Workspace permissions can affect how RLS is enforced.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/runni.title: Running Totals | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/runni.description: A running total accumulates a measure from a defined starting point through the maximum date in the current context. The filter logic must preserve the intended date scope.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/scatt.title: Scatter, Combo, Waterfall, and Specialized Visuals | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/scatt.description: Scatter plots show relationships between quantitative variables; combo charts combine compatible measures; waterfalls explain sequential contributions to change. Specialized visuals should be used only when their analytical purpose is clear.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/sched.title: Scheduled Refresh and Data Gateways | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/sched.description: Scheduled refresh updates imported semantic models. On-premises or private-network sources may require an on-premises data gateway. Credentials, privacy, capacity, and source availability affect refresh.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/selec.title: Select Columns and Filter Rows | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/selec.description: Early column and row reduction can simplify a model, reduce memory, and make later steps clearer. Filters must match the intended analytical population and should not hide source-quality issues without documentation.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/seman.title: Semantic Model Design Principles | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/seman.description: A semantic model organizes analytical tables, relationships, measures, hierarchies, formats, and metadata so report authors can ask consistent questions. Good models favor clear grain, reusable measures, understandable names, and predictable filtering.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/shari.title: Sharing, Export, and Governance | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/shari.description: Power BI supports sharing, app distribution, subscriptions, export, Analyze in Excel, and embedded consumption according to licensing and tenant settings. Every distribution method changes how data can be accessed or copied.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/slice.title: Slicers, Filters, and the Filter Pane | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/slice.description: Power BI supports visual, page, report, drillthrough, and slicer filters. Filter placement affects discoverability, consistency, and user interpretation.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/split.title: Split, Merge, and Custom Columns | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/split.description: Columns can be split by delimiter, position, or character transition; columns can be merged; custom columns can apply M expressions row by row.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/star-.title: Build a Star Schema | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/star-.description: A star schema places a fact table at the center and connects it to denormalized dimensions through one-to-many relationships. This design supports intuitive filtering, efficient compression, and understandable DAX.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/targe.title: Targets, Variance, and KPI Status | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/targe.description: Target analysis requires a target fact table at a defined grain, compatible dimensions, and measures for actual, target, variance, and status. Targets should not be repeated across detailed fact rows.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/text-.title: Text, Date, and Number Transformations | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/text-.description: Power Query provides transformations for trimming and cleaning text, changing case, extracting components, calculating date parts, rounding numbers, and applying arithmetic operations.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/varia.title: Variables and Readable DAX | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/varia.description: VAR stores a scalar or table result inside a DAX expression, and RETURN specifies the final result. Variables improve readability, debugging, and reuse within one calculation.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/visua.title: Edit Visual Interactions | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/visua.description: Selecting a data point can filter, highlight, or leave other visuals unchanged. Edit Interactions controls this behavior per visual pair.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/visua.title: Choose the Right Visual | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/visua.description: Visual selection begins with the analytical task: comparison, trend, distribution, relationship, composition, detail, or geography. Decoration should never override accurate encoding.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/welco.title: Welcome to Power BI for Data Analytics | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/welco.description: Power BI is Microsoft’s business analytics platform for connecting to data, transforming it, building governed semantic models, creating interactive reports, and sharing insights. Power BI Desktop is the main authoring application; the Power BI service supports publishing, collaboration, refresh, and governed consumption.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/works.title: Workspaces, Roles, and Collaboration | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/works.description: Workspaces organize content and use roles such as Admin, Member, Contributor, and Viewer to control collaboration. Workspace access is different from app audience access and row-level security.

/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/year-.title: YTD, QTD, and MTD Measures | Power BI for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/power-bi-data-analytics/year-.description: TOTALYTD, TOTALQTD, TOTALMTD, or CALCULATE with date functions can accumulate a base measure from the beginning of a period to the current date context.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/ab-test.title: A/B Test Analysis | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/ab-test.description: An A/B test compares outcomes between randomly assigned variants. Conversion analysis uses counts, rates, uncertainty, and practical impact.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/aggrega.title: Aggregation and Axis | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/aggrega.description: Aggregation functions reduce many values to summaries. The `axis` argument controls whether a calculation runs by row, column, or over all elements.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/array-s.title: Array Shape, Size, and dtype | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/array-s.description: Shape describes array dimensions, size counts elements, and dtype describes stored value representation.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/bar-cha.title: Bar Charts | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/bar-cha.description: Bar charts compare magnitudes across discrete categories using length from a common baseline.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/boolean.title: Boolean Masks and Filtering | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/boolean.description: A Boolean mask is an array of True and False values used to select matching elements.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/box-plo.title: Box Plots | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/box-plo.description: A box plot summarizes median, quartiles, spread, and candidate outliers.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/broadca.title: Broadcasting | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/broadca.description: Broadcasting lets NumPy combine arrays with compatible shapes without manually repeating values.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/clean-t.title: Clean Text and Categories | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/clean-t.description: Text cleaning standardizes case, whitespace, punctuation, and category mappings while preserving identifiers and meaning.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/comment.title: Comments, Docstrings, and Readable Style | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/comment.description: Readable analytical code uses descriptive names, small functions, consistent formatting, comments for reasoning, and docstrings for reusable interfaces.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/compari.title: Comparison and Logical Operators | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/compari.description: Comparison operators produce Boolean results. Logical operators combine conditions using `and`, `or`, and `not`.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/concat-.title: Concatenate Datasets | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/concat-.description: `concat` combines DataFrames vertically or horizontally. Vertical combination requires compatible schemas and deliberate source tracking.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/conditi.title: Conditional Statements | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/conditi.description: `if`, `elif`, and `else` choose which block of code runs based on ordered conditions.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/confide.title: Confidence Intervals with SciPy | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/confide.description: A confidence interval estimates a population parameter using a sample estimate and sampling uncertainty.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/correla.title: Correlation Analysis | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/correla.description: Correlation measures the direction and strength of association between numerical variables. It does not establish causation.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/create-.title: Create and Assign Columns | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/create-.description: New columns can be calculated from existing columns using vectorized expressions or `assign`.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/create-.title: Create DataFrames | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/create-.description: DataFrames can be created from dictionaries, lists of records, arrays, and many file formats.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/creatin.title: Create Arrays | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/creatin.description: NumPy creates arrays from Python collections or helper functions such as `arange`, `linspace`, `zeros`, and `ones`.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/data-ty.title: Data Types and Conversion | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/data-ty.description: pandas supports numeric, text, Boolean, categorical, and datetime types. Conversion functions can coerce invalid values to missing markers for review.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/datetim.title: Datetime Index and Time Series | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/datetim.description: A time series is ordered by time, often using a DatetimeIndex for slicing, resampling, and rolling analysis.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/descrip.title: Descriptive Statistics with pandas | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/descrip.description: pandas provides count, mean, median, standard deviation, quantiles, and categorical frequencies.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/detect-.title: Detect and Remove Duplicates | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/detect-.description: Duplicates must be evaluated at the correct business key. Entirely identical rows and repeated entities are different quality problems.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/detect-.title: Detect and Treat Outliers | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/detect-.description: Outliers are unusual values, not automatically errors. Statistical rules such as IQR fences identify candidates that require domain review.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/diction.title: Dictionaries and Key-Value Data | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/diction.description: A dictionary maps unique keys to values. It resembles a labeled record and is widely used for configuration, JSON-like data, and lookup logic.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/distrib.title: Analyze Distributions | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/distrib.description: Distribution analysis examines center, spread, shape, tails, and unusual values rather than relying on one average.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/eda-wor.title: Exploratory Data Analysis Workflow | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/eda-wor.description: EDA investigates structure, quality, distributions, relationships, and unusual cases before formal modeling or decisions.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/excepti.title: Exceptions and Defensive Code | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/excepti.description: Defensive code validates assumptions and raises or handles exceptions with useful messages.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/export-.title: Export DataFrames | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/export-.description: DataFrames can be written to CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet, and other formats. Index, encoding, data types, and formatting affect the output.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/filter-.title: Filter Rows | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/filter-.description: Boolean conditions filter DataFrame rows. Multiple conditions require parentheses and elementwise operators such as `&` and `|`.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/first-a.title: Build Your First Analytical Program | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/first-a.description: A useful first program takes a small set of values, computes a transparent metric, and prints an interpretation with units and limitations.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/for-loo.title: For Loops | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/for-loo.description: A `for` loop repeats a block for each item in an iterable.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/functio.title: Function Arguments and Defaults | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/functio.description: Functions can accept positional, keyword, and default arguments. Explicit keyword arguments improve readability when several values have similar types.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/functio.title: Functions and Return Values | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/functio.description: A function packages reusable logic behind a name, parameters, and a return value.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/groupby.title: GroupBy and Aggregation | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/groupby.description: The split-apply-combine pattern groups rows, applies summaries, and combines results.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/handle-.title: Handle Missing Values | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/handle-.description: Missing values can be removed, filled, modeled, or retained depending on why they are missing and how the field is used.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/histogr.title: Histograms | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/histogr.description: A histogram groups numerical values into bins to show distribution shape. Bin width affects the visible pattern.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/hypothe.title: Hypothesis Tests with SciPy | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/hypothe.description: A hypothesis test evaluates how compatible observed data are with a stated null model.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/.title: Python for Data Analytics Tutorial | Data Learning Hub
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/.description: A complete analyst-first Python tutorial covering Python foundations, Jupyter, NumPy, pandas, cleaning, transformation, exploratory analysis, statistics, Matplotlib, time series, reproducibility, browser practice, and a portfolio project.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/indexin.title: Index and Slice Arrays | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/indexin.description: Array indexing selects elements, rows, columns, or multidimensional regions. Slices usually create views rather than independent copies.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/inspect.title: Inspect a DataFrame | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/inspect.description: Initial inspection uses shape, column names, dtypes, sample rows, summary information, and missing-value counts.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/install.title: Install and Import Packages | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/install.description: Python packages extend the language. Analysts commonly use NumPy for arrays, pandas for tabular data, Matplotlib for visualization, and SciPy for scientific and statistical routines.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/install.title: Install Python and Create an Environment | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/install.description: A Python environment isolates the interpreter and packages used by one project. The course baseline is stable Python 3.14, while most examples remain compatible with recent Python 3 releases.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/jupyter.title: Jupyter Notebooks and Cells | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/jupyter.description: A Jupyter notebook combines narrative text, executable code, and output in an ordered document. Cell execution order matters because notebook state can differ from visual order.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/labels-.title: Labels, Legends, and Annotations | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/labels-.description: Titles, axis labels, legends, notes, and annotations give a chart the context needed for interpretation.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/line-ch.title: Line Charts | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/line-ch.description: Line charts show change over an ordered continuous axis, commonly time.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/list-co.title: List Comprehensions | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/list-co.description: A list comprehension creates a list from an iterable using a compact expression and optional condition.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/lists-a.title: Lists and Sequences | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/lists-a.description: A list is an ordered, mutable collection. Lists are useful for small collections, but tabular analytics usually belongs in NumPy arrays or pandas objects.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/logging.title: Logging and Quality Checks | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/logging.description: Logging records important workflow events; assertions and tests verify expected conditions.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/manage-.title: Manage Environments and Requirements | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/manage-.description: A requirements file or environment definition records project dependencies. Exact pins improve repeatability but require planned updates.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/matplot.title: Matplotlib Figure and Axes | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/matplot.description: A Matplotlib Figure is the full canvas and an Axes is one plotting area containing scales, labels, and artists.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/merge-a.title: Merge and Join DataFrames | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/merge-a.description: `merge` combines tables using keys and join types. Cardinality mistakes can duplicate facts and inflate metrics.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/method-.title: Method Chaining and Pipelines | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/method-.description: Method chaining expresses a sequence of DataFrame transformations as a readable pipeline.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/missing.title: Missing and Invalid Numbers | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/missing.description: Floating-point arrays can represent missing numeric values with `NaN`. Infinite values and invalid operations require separate checks.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/modules.title: Modules, pathlib, and Files | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/modules.description: The standard library provides modules for paths, CSV, JSON, dates, statistics, and many other tasks. `pathlib` creates platform-aware paths.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/numbers.title: Numbers, Booleans, and None | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/numbers.description: Python represents whole numbers with `int`, decimal numbers with `float`, logical values with `bool`, and absence with `None`.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/numpy-a.title: NumPy Arrays | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/numpy-a.description: A NumPy `ndarray` stores homogeneous numerical data in one or more dimensions.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/parse-d.title: Parse and Use Dates | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/parse-d.description: `to_datetime` converts date-like values into pandas datetime data, enabling date parts, sorting, resampling, and time differences.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/pivot-t.title: Pivot Tables and Crosstabs | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/pivot-t.description: `pivot_table` summarizes values by row and column categories; `crosstab` counts or normalizes category combinations.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/privacy.title: Privacy, Security, and Responsible Python | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/privacy.description: Analytical code can expose sensitive data through files, logs, notebooks, charts, or repository history.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/profile.title: Profile Data Quality | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/profile.description: A data-quality profile measures row counts, uniqueness, missingness, invalid types, ranges, categories, and duplicates before transformation.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.title: Portfolio Project Part 3: Analyze and Visualize | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.description: The analysis combines descriptive summaries, segment comparisons, time trends, distributions, relationships, and selected statistical methods.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.title: Portfolio Project Part 1: Brief and Questions | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.description: The final project begins with stakeholder questions, metric definitions, data inventory, assumptions, and acceptance criteria.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.title: Portfolio Project Part 2: Clean and Validate | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.description: The project must load source files, preserve raw data, profile quality, clean documented issues, and reconcile row counts and totals.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.title: Portfolio Project Part 4: Report and Publish | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.description: A portfolio-ready project includes source data references, a clean notebook, reusable code, output files, a README, findings, limitations, and instructions to reproduce the work.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.title: Python Scripts and Project Folders | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/python-.description: A script is a `.py` file executed from top to bottom. A clear project structure separates source data, notebooks, reusable code, outputs, and documentation.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/random-.title: Random Generation and Reproducibility | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/random-.description: NumPy random generators create simulated samples. A fixed seed or generator state makes a demonstration reproducible.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/read-cs.title: Read CSV Files | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/read-cs.description: `read_csv` parses delimited text into a DataFrame. Delimiter, encoding, headers, missing markers, date parsing, and data types affect the imported result.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/read-er.title: Read Errors and Tracebacks | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/read-er.description: A traceback records where an exception occurred and the chain of calls that led to it. Reading the final exception type and message is usually the fastest starting point.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/read-ex.title: Read Excel and JSON Data | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/read-ex.description: pandas reads spreadsheet sheets and JSON structures, but file layout and nested structure determine the correct options.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/rename-.title: Rename, Drop, and Reorder Columns | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/rename-.description: Column names can be standardized with `rename`; unnecessary columns can be removed with `drop`; lists control display order.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/reprodu.title: Reproducible Notebook Workflow | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/reprodu.description: A reproducible notebook runs from a clean kernel in order, records dependencies and data sources, and separates parameters, transformations, outputs, and conclusions.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/resampl.title: Resample Time Series | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/resampl.description: Resampling changes time frequency by grouping periods or generating new timestamps.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/reshape.title: Reshape with melt and pivot | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/reshape.description: Wide and long layouts serve different analytical tasks. `melt` converts repeated columns into rows; `pivot` reconstructs unique row-column combinations.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/respons.title: Responsible Chart Formatting | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/respons.description: Responsible formatting preserves proportional scales, readable labels, accessible contrast, and honest context.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/rolling.title: Rolling Windows and Moving Averages | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/rolling.description: A rolling window calculates each result from a moving set of recent observations.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/samplin.title: Sampling with Python | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/samplin.description: pandas can draw random or stratified samples. A sample is useful only when its selection process supports the intended population inference.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/save-an.title: Save and Export Figures | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/save-an.description: Matplotlib can save figures as raster or vector files with controlled size, resolution, background, and bounding box.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/scatter.title: Scatter Plots | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/scatter.description: Scatter plots show paired numerical values and help reveal direction, form, strength, clusters, and outliers.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/scope-a.title: Scope and Pure Functions | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/scope-a.description: Scope controls where a name can be accessed. A pure function depends only on its inputs and does not alter external state.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/segment.title: Compare Segments | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/segment.description: Grouped summaries compare categories while preserving counts, totals, rates, and uncertainty.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/select-.title: Select Columns | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/select-.description: Column selection returns a Series for one column or a DataFrame for a list of columns.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/select-.title: Select Rows with loc and iloc | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/select-.description: `loc` selects by labels and conditions; `iloc` selects by integer positions.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/series-.title: Series and DataFrames | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/series-.description: A pandas Series is a labeled one-dimensional array; a DataFrame is a labeled two-dimensional table with potentially different column types.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/sets-an.title: Sets and Unique Values | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/sets-an.description: A set stores unique unordered values and supports membership, union, intersection, and difference operations.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/simple-.title: Simple Linear Regression | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/simple-.description: Simple linear regression estimates a straight-line relationship between one predictor and one outcome.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/sort-va.title: Sort Values | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/sort-va.description: `sort_values` orders rows by one or more columns with independent ascending or descending directions.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/strings.title: Strings and Formatting | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/strings.description: Strings store text. Analysts clean, compare, split, normalize, and format strings when working with categories, identifiers, and report text.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/subplot.title: Subplots and Small Multiples | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/subplot.description: Subplots place multiple Axes in one Figure. Small multiples repeat a consistent chart across segments.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/transfo.title: Transform and Group-Level Calculations | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/transfo.description: `transform` returns a value aligned to each original row, enabling group totals, shares, and standardized values.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/tuples-.title: Tuples and Unpacking | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/tuples-.description: A tuple is an ordered immutable collection. Unpacking assigns its elements to multiple names and is useful for fixed records or function returns.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/validat.title: Validate Ranges and Business Rules | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/validat.description: Validation rules test allowed ranges, category sets, date order, and cross-field consistency.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/variabl.title: Variables and Assignment | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/variabl.description: A variable binds a name to an object. Assignment does not create a permanent spreadsheet cell; it makes a name refer to a value in the current program state.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/vectori.title: Vectorized Operations | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/vectori.description: Vectorization applies an operation to entire arrays without an explicit Python loop.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/welcome.title: Welcome to Python for Data Analytics | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/welcome.description: Python is a general-purpose programming language that analysts use to automate repeatable data work, inspect large datasets, apply statistical methods, and create reproducible outputs.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/while-l.title: While Loops and Control Flow | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/while-l.description: A `while` loop repeats while a condition remains true. `break` stops a loop and `continue` skips to the next iteration.

/tutorials/python-data-analytics/write-a.title: Write Analytical Outputs | Python for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/python-data-analytics/write-a.description: Analytical delivery can include cleaned data, summary tables, charts, notebooks, scripts, and a concise report.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/aggregate-.title: Aggregate Functions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/aggregate-.description: Aggregate functions summarize a set of rows into one result. COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX treat NULL values differently, so the measured field and population must be explicit.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/aggregatio.title: Aggregation Pitfalls | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/aggregatio.description: Aggregates can be wrong when joins multiply rows, filters exclude required records, or values are summarized at incompatible grains. A plausible total is not evidence of correctness.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/aliases-co.title: Aliases, Comments, and Readable Formatting | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/aliases-co.description: Aliases rename output columns or tables for clarity. Comments explain intent. Consistent indentation separates clauses and makes logic reviewable without changing the query result.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/and-or-not.title: Combine Conditions with AND, OR, and NOT | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/and-or-not.description: AND requires all connected predicates to be true. OR requires at least one. NOT reverses a condition. Parentheses make precedence explicit and protect the intended population.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/arithmetic.title: Arithmetic Expressions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/arithmetic.description: SQL expressions can add, subtract, multiply, divide, and combine stored values. Parentheses make business formulas explicit, and numeric type behavior should be checked to avoid unintended integer division or rounding.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/case-expre.title: CASE Expressions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/case-expre.description: CASE returns a value based on ordered conditions. The first matching WHEN branch wins, so ranges must be arranged carefully and an ELSE branch should handle unexpected values.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/coalesce-a.title: COALESCE and NULLIF | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/coalesce-a.description: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL value from a list. NULLIF returns NULL when two expressions are equal and is commonly used to prevent division by zero or convert placeholder values.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/cohort-ret.title: Cohort Retention with SQL | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/cohort-ret.description: Cohort analysis groups entities by a starting period and measures their activity in later periods. It requires a clear first-event rule and consistent period indexing.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/common-tab.title: Common Table Expressions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/common-tab.description: A common table expression, introduced with WITH, names an intermediate result for one statement. It can make a multi-stage analytical query easier to read and validate.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/comparison.title: Comparison Operators | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/comparison.description: Comparison operators test equality, inequality, and order. Text comparisons depend on collation and case rules, while numerical and date comparisons depend on valid data types.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/conditiona.title: Conditional Aggregation | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/conditiona.description: Conditional aggregation places CASE inside an aggregate to calculate several business conditions in one grouped query. Each condition should define its numerator and denominator clearly.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/correlated.title: Correlated Subqueries | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/correlated.description: A correlated subquery refers to columns from the current outer row and is logically evaluated in that row’s context. It can be expressive but may be slower than a join or window function.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/create-tab.title: CREATE TABLE, Data Types, and Constraints | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/create-tab.description: CREATE TABLE defines columns, data types, keys, and constraints. Constraints prevent invalid states closer to the source and document expected rules.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/cross-join.title: CROSS JOIN | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/cross-join.description: CROSS JOIN returns every combination of rows from two sources. The result count equals the product of the source row counts.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/customer-s.title: Project: Customer Segmentation | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/customer-s.description: Customer segmentation summarizes behavior at customer grain and assigns interpretable groups using order frequency, recency, and revenue.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/data-quali.title: Project: SQL Data Quality Audit | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/data-quali.description: A data quality audit combines structural checks, key checks, missing-value counts, referential integrity checks, and business-rule exceptions into a repeatable control report.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/date-and-t.title: Date and Time Functions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/date-and-t.description: Date functions extract calendar parts, shift periods, and calculate reporting buckets. PostgreSQL uses rich date types and functions; SQLite stores date text or numbers and uses functions such as strftime in the browser lab.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/deduplicat.title: Detect Duplicates with GROUP BY | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/deduplicat.description: Duplicate detection groups by the expected business key and keeps groups with more than one row. The correct key depends on the process, not only on a column named id.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/distinct-v.title: DISTINCT Values | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/distinct-v.description: DISTINCT removes duplicate combinations from the selected output columns. It does not repair duplicate source rows; it only changes the returned result.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/exists-sem.title: EXISTS, Semi Joins, and Anti Joins | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/exists-sem.description: EXISTS tests whether a related row exists without returning its columns. NOT EXISTS identifies base rows with no qualifying related rows.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/exists-sub.title: EXISTS Subqueries | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/exists-sub.description: EXISTS returns true as soon as a subquery finds a qualifying row. The selected expression inside EXISTS is not used; SELECT 1 is a common convention.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/final-sql-.title: Final Project: Retail SQL Analytics Portfolio | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/final-sql-.description: The final project turns a business question into a documented SQL analysis with schema review, quality checks, reusable query stages, metrics, segments, trends, and limitations.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/first-valu.title: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/first-valu.description: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE return boundary values within a window frame. LAST_VALUE often surprises learners because the default frame may end at the current row rather than the partition end.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/funnel-ana.title: Project: Funnel Analysis | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/funnel-ana.description: Funnel analysis counts users reaching ordered stages such as visit, product view, add to cart, and purchase. Stage definitions and time windows must be consistent.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/group-by/.title: GROUP BY | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/group-by/.description: GROUP BY partitions rows into groups with the same selected key values. Every selected expression should either define a group or be calculated with an aggregate.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/having/.title: Filter Groups with HAVING | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/having/.description: HAVING filters after groups and aggregate values have been calculated. WHERE filters source rows before grouping. Using the correct stage keeps the analytical population and group criteria separate.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/in-and-bet.title: IN and BETWEEN | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/in-and-bet.description: IN compares a value with a defined list. BETWEEN tests an inclusive lower and upper boundary. Both improve readability when the business rule naturally uses a set or range.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/.title: SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial | Data Learning Hub
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/.description: A complete analyst-first SQL tutorial using portable relational concepts, PostgreSQL-oriented explanations, and browser-side SQLite practice for querying, joining, aggregating, window functions, quality checks, and portfolio projects.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/indexes-an.title: Indexes and EXPLAIN | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/indexes-an.description: An index is a data structure that can speed selective lookups and joins while adding storage and write cost. EXPLAIN shows the execution plan chosen by the optimizer.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/inner-join.title: INNER JOIN | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/inner-join.description: INNER JOIN returns only row pairs that satisfy the join condition. Unmatched rows on either side are excluded.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/insert-upd.title: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE Safely | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/insert-upd.description: INSERT adds rows, UPDATE changes matching rows, and DELETE removes matching rows. UPDATE and DELETE without a correct WHERE clause can affect every row.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/join-debug.title: Debug and Reconcile Joins | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/join-debug.description: Join debugging compares row counts, distinct keys, unmatched records, and control totals before and after combination. The aim is to explain every change in grain.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/keys-and-r.title: Keys and Table Relationships | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/keys-and-r.description: Keys define identity and relationships. A primary key is unique within its table; a foreign key points to a related record. Join logic should use business-supported keys with compatible types.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/lag-and-le.title: LAG and LEAD | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/lag-and-le.description: LAG reads a value from a previous row and LEAD reads a later row within the window order. They avoid self joins for many period-over-period comparisons.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/left-join/.title: LEFT JOIN | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/left-join/.description: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table and adds matching values from the right. Right-side columns become NULL where no match exists.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/like-and-p.title: LIKE and Pattern Matching | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/like-and-p.description: LIKE matches text patterns. The percent sign represents any sequence of characters and the underscore represents one character. Pattern matching can be case-sensitive or insensitive depending on the system.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/logical-qu.title: Logical Query Processing Order | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/logical-qu.description: Although SELECT appears first in written SQL, a query is logically evaluated from its row sources and filters toward grouping, final selection, sorting, and limiting. This explains why some aliases are unavailable in WHERE.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/modular-qu.title: Modular Query Design | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/modular-qu.description: Modular SQL breaks a complex question into named, testable stages. Each stage should have a defined grain, purpose, and validation check.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/moving-ave.title: Moving Averages | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/moving-ave.description: A moving average summarizes a rolling set of recent periods. It smooths short-term variation but introduces lag and depends on a complete, ordered time series.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/multiple-d.title: Group by Multiple Dimensions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/multiple-d.description: Grouping by multiple columns creates one row for each unique combination. The number of output rows grows as dimensions become more detailed.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/multiple-t.title: Join Multiple Tables | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/multiple-t.description: Multi-table joins build a wider analytical dataset by following relationships through several tables. Each added relationship can change row count and grain.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/ntile-and-.title: NTILE and Percentile Bands | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/ntile-and-.description: NTILE assigns ordered rows to a requested number of approximately equal groups. It is useful for segmentation but may split equal values across groups.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/null-and-t.title: NULL and Three-Valued Logic | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/null-and-t.description: NULL represents a missing or unknown value, not zero or an empty string. Comparisons with NULL do not return true or false; they return unknown, so IS NULL and IS NOT NULL are required.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/order-by-l.title: ORDER BY, LIMIT, and OFFSET | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/order-by-l.description: ORDER BY defines result order. LIMIT restricts returned rows, and OFFSET skips rows. Without ORDER BY, a database does not guarantee a stable display sequence.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/practice-d.title: Explore the Practice Database Schema | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/practice-d.description: A schema describes tables, columns, keys, and relationships. Before writing analytical SQL, inspect the schema and identify the grain and join keys of every table you plan to use.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/ratios-per.title: Ratios, Percentages, and Average Order Value | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/ratios-per.description: A ratio divides a numerator by a denominator defined at a compatible grain. Casting and NULLIF protect decimal behavior and zero denominators.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/recursive-.title: Recursive CTEs | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/recursive-.description: A recursive CTE repeatedly references its own growing result until no new rows are produced. It normally contains an anchor query and a recursive query connected with UNION ALL.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/relational.title: Relational Databases and Tables | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/relational.description: A relational database stores data in tables. Each table represents one kind of entity or event, each row represents one occurrence, and each column represents one defined attribute.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/row-number.title: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, and DENSE_RANK | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/row-number.description: ROW_NUMBER assigns unique sequential positions. RANK gives ties the same rank and leaves gaps. DENSE_RANK gives ties the same rank without gaps.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/running-to.title: Running Totals | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/running-to.description: A running total accumulates a measure according to a defined order. The window frame should be explicit when duplicate sort values could affect results.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/sales-kpi-.title: Project: Sales KPI Scorecard | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/sales-kpi-.description: A scorecard query calculates a small set of clearly defined KPIs from validated order and item data. Each KPI needs a period, population, formula, and reconciliation rule.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/scalar-sub.title: Scalar Subqueries | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/scalar-sub.description: A scalar subquery returns one value and can be used in a comparison or selected expression. It must never return more than one row.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/select-fun.title: SELECT Fundamentals | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/select-fun.description: SELECT chooses the expressions and columns that will appear in a result. FROM identifies the source table. Selecting only required columns makes the result easier to read and usually reduces unnecessary data movement.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/self-join/.title: Self Joins | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/self-join/.description: A self join uses the same table twice with different aliases. It is useful when rows reference other rows in the same entity, such as employees and managers.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/sql-data-q.title: Profile Data Quality with SQL | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/sql-data-q.description: A quality profile counts missing values, duplicate keys, invalid categories, and suspicious ranges before analytical conclusions are produced. Profiling queries should be repeatable and saved with the project.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/sql-dialec.title: SQL Dialects: PostgreSQL and SQLite | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/sql-dialec.description: Core SQL ideas are portable, but database systems implement different functions, data types, date syntax, and administrative features. This course teaches PostgreSQL-oriented analytical SQL while the in-browser lab executes SQLite.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/star-schem.title: Star Schema for Analytics | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/star-schem.description: A star schema places measurable events in a fact table and descriptive context in dimension tables. A consistent grain and conformed dimensions support reliable reporting.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/string-fun.title: String Functions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/string-fun.description: String functions clean, combine, split, and standardize text. PostgreSQL and SQLite provide overlapping but not identical function names, so analysts should document the target dialect.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/subqueries.title: Subqueries in FROM | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/subqueries.description: A subquery in FROM creates a derived table that can be filtered, joined, or summarized by an outer query. It should have a meaningful alias.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/top-n-per-.title: Top N per Group | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/top-n-per-.description: Top-N-per-group ranks rows inside each partition and filters the rank in an outer query. This answers questions such as the top products in every category.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/transactio.title: Transactions | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/transactio.description: A transaction treats several changes as one unit. COMMIT makes them permanent; ROLLBACK cancels them. Atomicity protects the database from partial changes.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/type-conve.title: Type Conversion and CAST | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/type-conve.description: CAST converts an expression to a target data type when the database supports the conversion. Explicit conversion is safer than relying on implicit rules that may differ across systems.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/union-and-.title: UNION and UNION ALL | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/union-and-.description: UNION stacks compatible result sets and removes duplicates. UNION ALL stacks them without deduplication and is usually faster when duplicate preservation is correct.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/views/.title: Views | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/views/.description: A view stores a query definition and exposes it like a table. It centralizes repeated logic but does not automatically guarantee performance or correct governance.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/welcome-to.title: Welcome to SQL for Data Analytics | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/welcome-to.description: SQL is a declarative language for asking a relational database to return, combine, summarize, or change data. You describe the result you need; the database engine decides how to execute the request.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/where-filt.title: Filter Rows with WHERE | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/where-filt.description: WHERE keeps only rows whose condition evaluates to true. It is applied before grouping, which makes it the correct place to restrict dates, statuses, customers, or other row-level conditions.

/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/window-fun.title: Window Function Foundations | SQL for Data Analytics Tutorial
/tutorials/sql-data-analytics/window-fun.description: A window function calculates across related rows while preserving each row. The OVER clause defines the window, unlike GROUP BY which collapses rows.
